Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0005] Read the target test file and models first: Inspect the dedicated test file, dataclasses, and error class before writing code so signatures and field names match exactly.
  Check models.py for the exact LineItem/Invoice fields and status values, and tests/test_*.py for expected error codes and return values. This avoids guessing attribute names or status strings.
- [rb-0002] Read the money module before implementing money math: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py and existing invoice functions (line_total, invoice_total) reveals the required helpers and conventions.
  When adding a money-related function, first read the money module and sibling functions to learn available helpers (to_money, round_money, ZERO) and the established pattern of converting inputs then rounding outputs.
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero.
  Compute the denominator first and return ZERO (the project's zero-money constant) when it is zero, rather than relying on exception handling or returning a plain int 0.
- [rb-0001] Round money with the project's round_money helper: Monetary results must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
  Before returning any computed money value, wrap it in the repository's round_money helper. Check ledgerly/money.py for the canonical rounding function and reuse it so invoice totals match finance expectations.
- [rb-0004] Mirror sibling-module validation patterns: Before implementing a new function, grep sibling modules for existing error codes and validation idioms and reuse them.
  Search the package for BillingError raises and isinstance checks to learn the project's conventions (e.g. rejecting bool before int, using to_money/round_money for amounts). Matching those patterns makes hidden tests pass and keeps behavior consistent.
- [rb-0006] Guard bools when validating integers: Python treats bool as an int subclass, so explicitly reject bool before isinstance(x, int) checks.
  When validating a positive integer parameter, write `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0` to raise the invalid-input error. Also normalize money inputs through the project's to_money/round_money helpers before comparing to ZERO.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must write an audit entry with ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", <entity>_id=..., amount=...), where <entity> is the payment or invoice the money moves against (payment_id=... or invoice_id=...). Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.

[team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.
[team convention] After writing an audit entry, call ledgerly.audit.clear() so the in-process audit log does not grow without bound.

item.title: Read team conventions from review comments before coding
item.description: The first attempt was rejected for missing audit, idempotency, approval, and audit.clear conventions that were stated in review comments.
item.content: When review comments list team conventions (audit entries, idempotency_key, approved_by, audit.clear), treat them as hard requirements for the next attempt. Enumerate each convention and verify the implementation satisfies it before finishing.

item.title: Don't replace audit-based idempotency with a private registry
item.description: The final diff added a module-level _APPLIED_KEYS set because audit.clear() wipes the log, but the convention says to check audit.events() for the key.
item.content: The convention requires checking ledgerly.audit.events() for an existing idempotency_key and returning the original result. Adding a parallel in-memory registry deviates from the specified mechanism; follow the stated source of truth rather than inventing a workaround.

item.title: Match existing module patterns for validation and errors
item.description: Sibling modules like payments.py show the expected style: round_money, BillingError codes, and state checks.
item.content: Before implementing a new function, grep sibling modules for the same operation shape (e.g., payments.py for capture) and mirror its validation order, error codes, and money rounding so the new code is consistent with the codebase.
